objective: Help engineering leaders, architects, and AI platform teams build an explainable mental model of DeepSeek Harness, assess its extension model and enterprise evidence boundaries, position it in global and China markets, and define a reproducible next step.
audience: Engineering leaders, Agent platform architects, AI developers, and product strategists evaluating global and China markets
narrative: Begin with Harness as the control plane between a model and the real environment; explain the barrier-controlled Agent loop, Cordis, standing Preset scope, Session events, projection checkpoints, interfaces, SDKs, and dynamic Plugins; then separate local runtime, data paths, and enterprise evidence before mapping three global and China competitive layers and closing with a reproducible comparative study.

sections.title: Architecture: control, composition, and recoverable state
Extension: multiple interfaces and dynamic Plugins
Enterprise: safety primitives are not a control plane
Market: three global and China competitive layers

slides.purpose: Explain the Agent loop and its precise concurrency boundary.
slides.takeaway: Tool bodies may overlap, but exclusive barriers and ordered commits preserve deterministic model-visible order.
slides.title: A turn is a barrier-controlled feedback loop

body: Project context → Policy hooks → Model request
Tool choice → executionMode classification → exclusive barrier
Bodies may overlap → post-processing and tool/result commit in model order
Continue / stop / fail
data_points: Side-effect authority lives in Tool execution; concurrency does not imply unordered commits
content.speaker_notes: Exclusive calls create barriers and later calls are reclassified before they start. Only dispatch and Tool bodies may overlap; post-processing and Session result commits remain ordered.

visual.description: A seven-step loop with executionMode classification and an exclusive barrier; parallel Tool-body paths merge again at ordered commit.
visual.selection_reason: The diagram makes the slide's causal or comparative structure visible and directly supports the takeaway.

source.credit: Diagram synthesized from Agent loop and Session documentation

visual.alt_text: The Agent loop classifies Tool execution modes, limits overlap with exclusive barriers, and commits results in model order.

slides.purpose: Introduce the five Cordis runtime primitives.
slides.takeaway: Cordis puts capabilities, dependencies, events, and lifecycle in one Context tree.
slides.title: Five primitives turn plugin conventions into runtime rules

body: Context: visibility and lifecycle boundary
Service: stable dependency contract
Event: collaboration and interception
Effect: registration with a disposer
Scope: ownership for one activation
data_points: Reversible registration ≠ automatic compensation for external side effects
content.speaker_notes: Context is the center; Service and Event are discovered within it; Effect makes registration disposable; Scope decides ownership. External file or network effects still need compensation.

visual.description: Context, Service, Event, Effect, and Scope orbit a central Plugin runtime; a warning marks external effects outside automatic rollback.
visual.selection_reason: The diagram makes the slide's causal or comparative structure visible and directly supports the takeaway.

slides.purpose: Correct the lifecycle model for Host, Preset, and Session composition.
slides.takeaway: A Preset is a shared standing scope; the Session is the runtime instance that joins it.
slides.title: Presets are shared standing scopes; Sessions are instances

body: Host plane: Web, persistence, credentials, sandbox, providers
Agent Preset: one standing mount per process
Session Agent scope: parent → selected Preset
Switching: agent-preset/selected event, not a rewritten creation header
data_points: Mutable state in a shared Preset must be keyed by Session or another explicit owner
content.speaker_notes: Do not model a Preset as remounted for every Session. Multiple Session Agent scopes may parent to one standing scope, so shared mutable state needs explicit ownership.

visual.description: Host plane above one standing Agent Preset scope; two Session Agent scopes parent to it and each records a selection event.
visual.selection_reason: The diagram makes the slide's causal or comparative structure visible and directly supports the takeaway.
visual.alt_text: Two independent Session Agent scopes inherit capabilities from one shared standing Agent Preset scope.

slides.purpose: Explain ordered Profile configuration layering.
slides.takeaway: Effective capability comes from ordered overlays, with later patches closer to the current user and run.
slides.title: Four ordered layers—not one file—define the runtime

body: 1 · Bundles: reusable defaults
2 · Profile patch: product or role selection
3 · Home patch: durable user override
4 · --patch: temporary run override
data_points: Later layers override earlier ones · order is behavior
content.speaker_notes: Treat the layers as transparent sheets. Debugging requires provenance for every layer, not only the final JSON, or a Tool or policy override cannot be explained.

visual.description: Four translucent configuration sheets overlay one another, with --patch highlighted and Effective runtime at the output.
visual.selection_reason: The diagram makes the slide's causal or comparative structure visible and directly supports the takeaway.
visual.alt_text: Bundles, Profile patch, Home patch, and CLI patch form the effective runtime in order.

slides.purpose: Explain Session events, projection checkpoints, and replay.
slides.takeaway: Events are facts; the cache stores replayable unit state, not a persisted UI view.
slides.title: Events are facts; cache is versioned unit state

body: Events: user, assistant, Tool, approval, error
Request metadata: request/header · request/context
Checkpoint row: (key, ver, seq, val)
View: restore or re-view unit state + replay tail
content.speaker_notes: The cache stores versioned projection unit state. A cold read restores that state and replays events after seq to produce current Conversation, Tasks, or Usage views.

visual.description: An append-only event stream feeds a versioned checkpoint row, then tail replay generates Conversation, Tasks, and Usage views.

slides.purpose: Explain capability seams and their important cardinality and dependency exceptions.
slides.takeaway: A stable seam separates capability contract, implementations, consumers, and composable policy.
slides.title: Capability seams isolate Agents from implementations

body: Definition: stable types, methods, and events
Provider: one selected implementation or a named multi-provider registry
Consumer: Tool, Agent loop, UI, or another Service
Boundary exception: tool-fs-search uses subprocess/ripgrep, not ctx.fs
content.speaker_notes: The three-role model describes dependency direction, not provider count. Subagent hosts multiple named Providers, while filesystem search crosses the subprocess seam.

slides.purpose: Explain the dynamic Plugin release and rendering boundaries.
slides.takeaway: A dynamic Plugin is a page-mediated release system; activation and later rendering have separate success boundaries.
slides.title: Run ok does not guarantee the next Client render

body: Inspect: list → minimal query
Define: immutable Plugin / Package
Client half: wait for a matching page
Run: approval → starting → ok / failed
After settle: render diagnostics may still fail
data_points: Repair = new Package · Rollback = explicit currentPackageId
content.speaker_notes: A Client half can wait without a matching page. After Run ok, later rendering may fail independently, so inspect both Run diagnostics and post-settle render diagnostics.

slides.purpose: Separate runtime location, data paths, and enterprise control evidence.
slides.takeaway: Private deployment must independently prove where code runs, where data flows, and who governs access and lifecycle.
slides.title: Self-hosted answers only one of three questions

body: Layer 1 · Runtime local: where do code and processes run?
Layer 2 · Data path: where do models, search, Plugins, and telemetry go?
Layer 3 · Control evidence: who can access, approve, audit, upgrade, and own outcomes?
data_points: Harness: Layer 1 has primitives · Layer 2 is configurable · Layer 3 lacks public evidence
content.speaker_notes: Default Web search can create outbound traffic, and enabled OTel has a broad data surface. Enterprise claims require deployment-specific evidence rather than inference from self-hosting.

slides.purpose: Expose the exact boundaries of built-in safety primitives.
slides.takeaway: A file sandbox cannot establish network, process, credential, identity, or audit guarantees.
slides.title: Sandbox covers file effects and same-world only

body: Sandbox: file effects + same-world; Windows leaves read/network/process visible
Credentials: 0700/0600 does not block same-UID Tools
Telemetry: off by default; when on can include prompts, Tools, files, commands, and cwd
Outbound: Web search on by default; fetch and Session FTS off
Persistence / Web: JSONL is not auto-deleted; Host/Origin fence is not auth
data_points: Fail-closed ≠ full isolation · Append-only ≠ tamper-evident audit
content.speaker_notes: State limits precisely rather than calling the project secure or insecure. macOS also depends on deprecated sandbox-exec, and the bare Web server supplies no TLS or authentication.

visual.description: Six boundaries—Sandbox, Credentials, Telemetry, Outbound, Persistence, and Web—surround Agent, each labeled covered and not covered.
visual.selection_reason: The diagram makes the slide's causal or comparative structure visible and directly supports the takeaway.

source.credit: Boundary synthesis from sandbox, credential, telemetry and Web READMEs

visual.alt_text: Six boundaries around the Agent show what file sandboxing, credentials, telemetry, outbound access, persistence, and Web trust do and do not cover.

slides.purpose: Turn public evidence gaps into an enterprise verification agenda.
slides.takeaway: Enterprise adoption depends on verified identity, isolation, audit, and lifecycle evidence—not on plugin count.
slides.title: The enterprise gap is evidence and accountability

body: Identity / tenancy: Host fence → SSO, RBAC, workspace isolation
Execution: file sandbox → network/process/remote isolation
Secrets / data: local file → Vault/KMS, DLP, residency evidence
Audit: Session log → redaction, retention, tamper evidence
Lifecycle: developer preview → LTS, SBOM, CVE, SLA, support
data_points: Priority: High · Evidence status: Public gap
content.speaker_notes: This is a gap assessment based on reviewed public materials, not a compliance verdict. A deployment or commercial offering may add controls, so buyers must verify the actual system and contract.

slides.purpose: Define a reproducible comparison method.
slides.takeaway: Freeze the evaluator, use a unique run ID, and retain the full evidence bundle.
slides.title: Freeze grader, run ID, and evidence bundle

body: Choose: same-layer peer + deterministic task
Freeze: commit, model, Tools, network, budget, grader
Run: use a new run_id whenever the patch changes
Capture: summary + report.json + test_output.txt + run_instance.log + eval.sh + patch.diff
Score: outcome, recovery, safety, effort, efficiency
data_points: One success = case study; repeated tasks approach a benchmark
content.speaker_notes: Compare runtime architecture with AgentScope and developer workflow with Qwen Code. Freeze evaluator definitions and avoid SWE-bench-style cache reuse by changing run_id with every patch.

visual.description: Choose and Freeze split into System A and System B; a unique run-ID gate precedes Evidence bundle, Shared rubric, Explain, and Repeat.
visual.selection_reason: The diagram makes the slide's causal or comparative structure visible and directly supports the takeaway.

source.credit: Evaluation protocol synthesized from curriculum and evaluation guidance

visual.alt_text: Two systems run against frozen tasks and graders under unique run IDs, then produce a full evidence bundle for shared scoring and repetition.

slides.purpose: Close with a decision path that turns architectural interest into evidence.
slides.takeaway: Harness is worth studying for control-plane design; adoption depends on enterprise evidence and real-task outcomes.
slides.title: Turn architectural attention into governed adoption

body: 30 days: reproduce Profiles, Sessions, and capability seams
60 days: map security data flows and enterprise evidence gaps
90 days: run controlled comparisons with AgentScope and Qwen Code
Decision gate: embed, extend, partner, or wait based on evidence
data_points: Architecture attention → Reproducible evidence → Governed adoption
content.speaker_notes: Do not use stars as a buying decision. Use the 90-day evidence plan to convert technical interest into a reviewable conclusion.
